To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
B cells play a critical role in the development and maintenance of EAE and MS, and that B-cell depletion is an effective therapeutic strategy for the treatment of EAE and possibly MS.
the treatment of MS with IFN-β reduces the production of Th17 cells and the expression of the Th17 cytokine IL-17, but increases the production of Th1 cells and the expression the Th1 cytokine IFN-γ.
B-cell depletion with anti-CD20 therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis results in a reduction of the brain atrophy rate, which is not seen with interferon-β treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pathogenicity of the B-cell response in MS.
the role of B-cells in MS and their potential as therapeutic targets.
the role of T and B lymphocyte responses in MS, and with the potential use of immunotherapy in the treatment of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interferon beta has a beneficial role in the treatment of relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis and that it is the most studied and the most effective disease modifying treatment.
the evidence for interferon beta in MS is not strong enough for it to be recommended as first-line treatment for the condition.
interferon-beta has been shown to slow the rate of progression in MS, but the long-term impact on disability progression is uncertain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system is not a simple binary of Th1 and Th2, but that there are many different subsets of T-cells that are involved in the pathogenesis of MS.

we have demonstrated that B cells and their antibodies have a key role in the pathology of multiple sclerosis, and we have demonstrated that targeting B cells and/or their antibodies can be an effective therapeutic strategy for the treatment of multiple sclerosis.
‘B-cell strategies’ are the future of MS therapy, and that we should be moving towards a ‘Th2-dependent’ approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B cells play an important role in multiple sclerosis.
we have a new tool for studying the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis.
the immune system is very complex and there are a lot of different players in the immune system.
